objective: Put the qualified Zig engine on the host and close the drift it left behind. Two paths were used, and the difference between them is the finding of this run.

steps.name: manual-deploy
steps.detail: 18:36 local: the four freshly built files were installed straight into /usr/lib/calix with pkexec install, after snapper snapshot #2518. The daemon and notifier were then restarted so they stopped running deleted inodes.
steps.finding: The files landed, and nothing recorded that they had: pacman still described a package whose contents were replaced underneath it. This is the failure mode of installing by copy.

steps.name: drift-measured
steps.detail: pacman -Qkk calix-gpui-git: 61 total files, 4 altered — exactly the four files installed by hand, on a package the database still reported at r4874.gaaa19992 while the disk held a newer build.

steps.name: package-built
steps.detail: 19:47-19:52 local: makepkg in .ci-cache/pkg from the repository's PKGBUILD-calix (source git+https branch=main), pinned Zig 0.16.0. Result: calix-gpui-git r5001.g5e5225ae-1. The package carries the engine, the GPUI frontend, the flatpak backend, the units, the polkit policy and the desktop files.

steps.name: package-installed
steps.detail: pkexec pacman -U replaced r4874.gaaa19992 with r5001.g5e5225ae-1. pacman's own hooks took the transaction's pre/post snapshots (2522/2523), which makes hand-taken pairs redundant for a pacman transaction.

steps.name: acceptance
steps.detail: pacman -Qkk: 61 files, 0 altered. Daemon and notifier restarted, each /proc/<pid>/exe a live inode whose sha256 equals the installed binary. IPC ping and status answered on daemon.sock. calix health exit 0. calix-gpui --help answers.

defect_found_and_fixed.defect: The package had no install scriptlet, so pacman -U left calix-daemon and calix-notify running the inodes they were started from. Nothing in the transaction said so.
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: calix-gpui-git.install added: post_install/post_upgrade restart the user units of every logged-in user through `systemctl --user -M user@`. `scripts/package-build` became the single staging point so the PKGBUILD and its scriptlet cannot be copied out of step; `scripts/install-machine` now verifies the running inode's hash instead of only asserting a PID exists.
